newsitem.title: USA: Physical nickel market unaffected by LME rally.
newsitem.headline: Physical nickel market unaffected by LME rally.

text.p: The physical market appeared to be unaffected by the recent run in nickel prices, although premiums have edged up slightly.
The LME three-month nickel price rose $610 to $7,385 a tonne, or $3.35 a lb, over the last two trading days. Spot premiums are up to 12-13 cents over LME cash from 9-11 cents last week.

"There's nothing about the physical market at $7,300 that was any different from where it was at $6,700," said one New York dealer. "We're still booking business. The large mills haven't jumped in yet. But we're seeing buying from some of the smaller foundries."
"I think this is just a technical correction," said another merchant. "Physical business has been pretty quiet."
